title: DOJ Epstein disclosure redaction dispute
summary: A federal judge ordered DOJ to produce less-redacted Epstein records or explain why additional material remains withheld. DOJ has argued that redactions and withholdings are appropriate under its legal position.
evidenceBoundary: This trigger tracks disclosure, redaction and court-compliance questions. It does not treat a redacted name, withheld document or public mention as evidence of wrongdoing by itself.

sourceRoutes.label: Court docket and order
sourceRoutes.needed: Judge order, DOJ response, docket entry, redaction log or explanation.

sourceRoutes.label: Official DOJ filing
sourceRoutes.needed: DOJ explanation for withheld records and redaction categories.

sourceRoutes.label: Media route
sourceRoutes.needed: Use only to route readers to court filings; do not use media summary as final proof.

questions: Which exact files remain withheld or more heavily redacted?
Did DOJ provide a redaction log or category explanation?
Which redactions protect victims, minors, privacy or law-enforcement interests?
Which redactions concern non-victim names, institutional routes, communications or accountability-relevant facts?
What does the judge do after reviewing DOJ's explanation?

affectedScenarios.reason: Official disclosure dispute increases relevance of institution-level fallout before person-level clarity.
Missing and redacted records become central investigation map.
Public trust and verification demand rises when disclosure conflicts remain unresolved.

nextAction: Add this trigger to the live Trigger Watchtower, record intake queue and probability signal feed.
